tytul: Kombucha with black and green tea (NCHFP recipe)
wstep: This card describes the NCHFP kombucha recipe, made with black and green tea, sugar and a SCOBY, and kept in the refrigerator after fermentation. [T:NAP-087,NAP-003]

akapity: Before you start, the pH of the starter liquid must be 4.0 or less; if it is greater than 4.0, do not make kombucha with that starter. [T:NAP-001]
Do not use glazed ceramic (earthenware) containers for fermenting or storing kombucha, because the acidic drink can leach heavy metals. [T:NAP-007]
Storing kombucha in airtight containers builds up carbon dioxide and can lead to an explosion if it is not checked regularly. [T:NAP-004]
NCHFP uses 1 gallon of water, divided, 3 tablespoons (or 6 tea bags) of black tea and 1/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons (or 13 tea bags) of green tea. [T:NAP-087]
It also uses 1 cup of granulated sugar and 1 SCOBY with its starter liquid. [T:NAP-087]

Guidelines for producers from the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets say to use a commercially purchased culture (SCOBY) for the first batch; later batches may be started from earlier ones only if they show no mold or unusual contamination. [T:NAP-020]
No washing, boiling or other treatment removes lead from ceramics, and a poorly fired glaze can release lead into food and drinks. [T:NAP-009]
Clean the kitchen area and wash your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds. [T:NAP-088]
Wash and rinse the equipment, then submerge it in hot water of at least 171 °F (about 78 °C) for at least 30 seconds to sanitize it. [T:NAP-088]
Put 1 tablespoon of the starter liquid in a small bowl and test it with a pH strip or litmus paper, following the test paper maker’s instructions. [T:NAP-089]
If the pH is 4.0 or less, continue, and discard the sample you tested. [T:NAP-001,NAP-089]
If the pH is greater than 4.0, do not make kombucha with this starter liquid. [T:NAP-001]
Heat 4 cups of the water to 160–170 °F (about 71–77 °C), checking it with a food thermometer, and steep the tea for 2 minutes. [T:NAP-088]
Remove or strain the tea, pour it into the fermentation container, add the sugar and stir until it dissolves. [T:NAP-088]
Add 12 cups of cold water. [T:NAP-088]
The tea must be below 95 °F (35 °C) before you add the SCOBY and starter liquid. [T:NAP-006]
Add the SCOBY and starter liquid and stir well for 10 seconds. [T:NAP-089]
Dry the opening of the container and cover it with a paper towel, coffee filter or clean cheese cloth, secured with a rubber band or string. [T:NAP-089]
Mark the container with the date; this is day 0 of fermentation. [T:NAP-089]
Ferment the kombucha at room temperature, 68–77 °F (20–25 °C), for 7–10 days. [T:NAP-002]
The recommended pH of finished kombucha is between 2.5 and 4.2. [T:NAP-015]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): on day 7, test the pH of the kombucha with a pH strip, as NCHFP describes for the starter liquid. [T:NAP-018,NAP-089]
If the kombucha does not reach a pH of 4.2 or lower within 7 days, the culture is probably contaminated or the temperature too low, and the batch should be discarded. [T:NAP-018]
Fermenting for more than 10 days can raise the acidity of kombucha to a potentially harmful level. [T:NAP-017]
When fermentation is complete, pour the kombucha into clean, sanitized jars or bottles, refrigerate it promptly and use it within 30 days. [T:NAP-003]

If you mix other ingredients into kombucha after fermentation, drink it immediately or keep it in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; the NCHFP recipe does not cover a second fermentation in a closed bottle. [T:NAP-005]
Under some conditions the alcohol content can exceed 0.5% by volume, the US TTB limit for a non-alcoholic drink. [T:NAP-010]
Dry, fuzzy spots, white or colored, on the SCOBY or on the surface of the kombucha mean that it has spoiled; discard both the drink and the SCOBY. [T:NAP-021]
UGA Extension considers up to 4 fluid ounces (about 120 ml) of kombucha a day safe for most healthy people. [T:NAP-022]
UGA Extension does not recommend kombucha for people prone to acidosis, people with weakened immunity, or pregnant or breastfeeding women. [T:NAP-022]
